title: I'm eating
goal: Say what is happening right now and what has changed — and clear up the biggest misunderstanding about Mandarin: 了 is not a past tense.
bekal: use 在 before a verb to say something is "in progress"
use 了 correctly — as a marker of change, not of the past
negate events with 沒 and drop 了 when you do

dialogs.title: 對話 — 電話裡的午餐
dialogs.intro: Xiaomei calls Budi around midday. Budi is in the middle of something.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Hello? Budi, what are you doing?
lines.literal: hello? Budi, you — (in progress) — do — what?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Not yet. I'm still in class.
lines.literal: still — not. I — still — (in progress) — attend-class.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [妳|Nǐ][不是|bú shì][三點|sān diǎn][下課|xiàkè][嗎|ma]？[現在|Xiànzài][四點|sì diǎn][了|le]。
lines.id: Doesn't your class end at three? It's already four.
lines.literal: you — not-be — three — o'clock — end-class — (question)? now — four — o'clock — (change).

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: The professor ran over time! I'm about to starve to death.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][幫|bāng][妳|nǐ][買|mǎi][一個|yí ge][便當|biàndāng][好嗎|hǎo ma]？
lines.id: Shall I buy you a lunch box?
lines.literal: I — help — you — buy — one — (measure word) — lunch-box — good — (question)?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: That'd be great! You're so sweet!

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: What do you want? Pork chop or chicken leg?
lines.literal: you — want — what? rib-bone — or — chicken-leg?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: OK. As soon as I finish eating I'll go buy it.
lines.literal: good. I — eat — finish — then — go — buy.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Class is over! I'm coming to find you now.
lines.literal: end-class — (change)! I — now — pass-go — look-for — you.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: OK, I'll wait for you in the cafeteria.
lines.literal: good, I — at — student — restaurant — wait — you.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][五分鐘|wǔ fēnzhōng][到|dào]！[不要|Bú yào][吃|chī][完|wán][喔|o]！
lines.id: I'll be there in five minutes! Don't eat it all!
lines.literal: I — five — minute — arrive! not — want — eat — finish — (softener)!

notes: **喂 (*wéi*) is only used to answer the phone**, never to greet someone standing in front of you. The tone usually rises to *wéi*, even though dictionaries write *wèi*.
**拖堂 ("dragging the class") means a teacher who doesn't stop on time** — a word every Taiwanese student knows. Its opposite, 提早下課 (finishing early), is greeted with cheers.
⚠️ **快…了 means "almost", "any minute now"**: 快餓死了 (starving to death), 快到了 (almost there), 快下雨了 (it's about to rain). The frame is complete with 了 at the end and can't be split.
**餓死了 ("hungry to death") is the everyday Taiwanese way to exaggerate**: 熱死了 (so hot), 累死了 (so tired), 笑死了 (LOL). It isn't rude at all.
⚠️ **完 after a verb means "finished, used up"**: 吃完 (finish eating), 看完 (finish reading), 做完 (finish doing). It's a result complement — a form covered fully in unit 18.

grammars.title: 在 + verb: in progress
body: To say that something is happening **right now**, put **在** directly in front of the verb. That's it; the verb itself doesn't change at all.

head: Sentence
Pīnyīn
Meaning
rows: I'm in class right now. (more emphatic)
Wǒ méi yǒu zài kàn diànshì.

after: ⚠️ **Don't confuse it with 在 meaning "at" from unit 7.** The difference is simple: **在 + place** = at a place; **在 + verb** = in progress. When both appear together, the place wins: *我在圖書館看書* (I'm reading at the library) — and 在 appears only once.
**正在 is more emphatic than 在** and stresses "at this very moment". In everyday conversation, 在 alone is enough.

grammars.title: ⚠️ 了 is not a past tense
body: This is the biggest misunderstanding almost every beginner brings along, and it's an understandable one: textbooks often translate 了 as "already" or treat it as the past tense. What 了 really marks is **change** — something that wasn't so before and is now; or something that has been completed.
Proof that it isn't a past tense: past sentences often come **without** 了, and future sentences often come **with** 了.

head: Sentence
Pīnyīn
Meaning
Time
rows: Wǒ míngtiān dào le zài dǎ gěi nǐ.
I'll call you tomorrow once I arrive.
As a child I lived in Tainan.

after: ⚠️ **The most important rule in this unit: 了 DISAPPEARS when the sentence is negated.** *我吃了* → *我沒吃*, not *我沒吃了*. This mistake is very common and very easy to fix — memorize it now.
**還沒 = "not yet"**, and it's the most common answer to questions with the pattern 你…了嗎？ *你吃了嗎？* → *還沒。*
**Asking with 了: …了嗎？ or …了沒？** The second form is very Taiwanese and sounds casual: *你吃了沒？* It's even used as a greeting, much like "How's it going?" in English.

blocks.title: The "what are you up to?" patterns you'll use every day
items: **你在做什麼？** — What are you up to? (the most common question in messaging apps)
**我在回家的路上。** — I'm on my way home.
**我在等你。** — I'm waiting for you.
⚠️ The short reply **在忙** ("busy") is the politest way of saying "I'll get back to you later".

sections.title: Three ways to use 了, and one prohibition

blocks.text: Compare these two sentences until you feel the difference: **我餓了** means "I've gotten hungry" — I wasn't before, now I am. **我很餓** means "I'm hungry" — just a state, with no story of change. English often translates both as "I'm hungry", and that's exactly where 了 slips out of a beginner's head.

sections.title: The lunch box: a culture lesson in one box

blocks.text: **便當 (*biàndāng*) is a loanword from Japanese *bentō*** — a legacy of fifty years of Japanese rule in Taiwan, and one of hundreds of Japanese words still alive here. It's the standard lunch all over Taiwan: rice, one main dish, three or four vegetable sides, all in one box for 80–100 塊.
⚠️ **Soup and extra rice are usually free at Taiwanese 便當 shops**, and the seller may genuinely be hurt if you turn them down thinking you'd have to pay. Just take them, and say 謝謝.

exercises.prompt: Negate the sentences — remember what happens to 了.
Fill in with 在, 了, or 還沒.
items: 我 ____ 吃飯，等一下打給你。
我 ____ 做完，再給我十分鐘。

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: 什麼 / 做 / 你 / 在
嗎 / 吃 / 你 / 了

answers: 你在做什麼？ — 我在吃飯。 — 你吃了嗎？ — 還沒。 — 現在四點了。 — 快下雨了。
我沒吃。 — 他沒去。 — 我沒買書。 — 她沒來。 — 我沒看那部電影。
在 — 了 — 還沒 — 了 — 在 — 還沒
你在做什麼？ — 我在吃飯。 — 你吃了嗎？ — 現在四點了。 — 快到了。
